titleEn: Watch for Bikes Before You Cross!

pages.text: "Let's go to the water! Let's find shells!" Pongi hopped in the doorway. Mom, wearing her headscarf, followed with a basket. The water sparkled beyond the path on the bank.
Seeing the water made Pongi hurry even more. "There it is! I'll cross quickly!" Without looking either way, she stepped onto the bicycle path. Mom quickly gripped her paw. "Pongi, wait!"
Ring, ring! A bicycle whizzed right past Pongi's nose. The neighbor riding it called, "Careful!" Pongi's mouth opened round. Her heart thumped.
Mom crouched in front of Pongi and held her paws. "Bicycles whizz along this path. However much we hurry, our safety rules come first." Pongi nodded. "What rules?"
"Let's play turn-your-head! You can see bicycles from far away." Mom looked left and right. Pongi copied her. A bicycle looked tiny in the distance. Mom sang, "Watch for bikes before you cross!"
Mom taught her three rules. "One, stop at the path! Two, look left and right for bicycles! Three, raise one paw, hold Mom with the other, and cross!" Pongi clenched both paws. "I can do it too!"
When the path grew quiet, Pongi stopped and looked left and right. She raised one paw and crossed the middle of the path with steady steps. "Watch for bikes before you cross!" Her voice was brave.
Safe at the water! Pongi thumped her tail on the bank. "I did all three by myself!" Mom clapped her paws. Water rippled beneath their feet.

After collecting lots of shells, they headed home. This time Pongi led the way and stopped at the path. "One, stop! Two, look left and right for bicycles! Three, raise one paw, hold Mom with the other, and cross!" Mom smiled behind her.

At home, Mom hugged Pongi tight. "You stopped for the bicycle bell. Well done, Pongi!" However much she hurries, the rules come first when crossing the path. Pongi grinned. "Watch for bikes before you cross!"
